newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ROMARIO RETURNS TO BRAZIL WITH 13 SUITCASES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMARIO RETURNS TO BRAZIL WITH 13 SUITCASES.

text.p: Tempestuous striker Romario, who is hoping to rejoin Rio de Janeiro club Flamengo, returned to Brazil on Tuesday with all his luggage, a club spokesman said.

Romario, who hired a minivan to transport his 13 suitcases from the airport to his luxury flat, vowed not to play for Spanish club Valencia again while Luis Aragones was coach, Flamengo spokesman Altair Baffa said.
"He says he is not going back while Aragones is still there," he said.
Valencia beat Slavia Prague 1-0 away in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday without Romario's help.
Romario, who joined the Spanish club only in August, was dropped from the team by Aragones for the second time last week after oversleeping and arriving late for training.
Flamengo president Kleber Leite travelled to Spain on Sunday to open negotiations with Valencia to bring back the unhappy striker, who has already been back to Brazil twice since moving to Valencia.
Baffa said that Valencia wanted $750,000 to loan Romario to Flamengo until mid-1997 but that Flamengo, beset by a financial crisis, did not have the money and were offering them players in exchange.
The attempt to bring back Romario is a last desperate bid by Leite to save their Brazilian championship campaign from disaster.
Flamengo began the competition, in which the top eight teams qualify for the quarter-finals, fairly strongly but have lost their last four games, three of them by a score of 4-1.
If Romario returns, he will line-up alongside his World Cup striking partner Bebeto in attack.
